pages.text: North Dakota Badlands 2026: When to visit, where to stay, and what to do | National Geographic TRAVEL BEST OF THE WORLD Why you should visit the rugged North Dakota Badlands in 2026 Discover the best seasons to visit, where to stay near Theodore Roosevelt National Park, and how to explore this otherworldly landscape. The Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library is set to open in July 2026 outside Medora, North Dakota. Photograph by Image Professionals GmbH, Alamy Stock Photo By Stephanie Pearson Published October 21, 2025 Theodore Roosevelt first traveled to the Badlands on a hunting trip in 1883. He was so taken by the otherworldly landscape of pastel buttes, trilling meadowlarks, and disappearing bison, that he returned in 1884 to grieve the simultaneous deaths of his wife and mother, raising cattle and working on the wild frontier for almost three years. Its “desolate, grim beauty” so changed Roosevelt that he famously wrote, “I would not have been president had it not been for my experience in North Dakota .” Opening on July 4, 2026, the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library celebrates the Badlands as much as it does the 26th president. Designed by Norwegian architectural firm Snøhetta, the state-of-the-art, sustainable library sits high on a lonely butte outside of Medora, a military camp turned frontier town named after a French nobleman’s wife. The 93,000-square-foot library disappears into its surroundings, camouflaged by a living roof sprouting native plants, part of a 1.3-mile walking trail that provides sweeping views toward the national park. pages.text: Northern Ireland 1-0 Ukraine: The 'manager's dream' who has put NI one game from history - BBC Sport Image source, Press Eye Image caption, Terry Devlin scored his first Northern Ireland goal against Ukraine By Andy Gray BBC Sport NI Journalist Published 14 November 2026 It was a moment that Northern Ireland needed. When Terry Devlin picked the ball up on the edge of the area in the 68th minute against Ukraine there was only one thought in his mind. And when the ball flew into the corner Windsor Park erupted at another highlight of a Nations League campaign that has been a real feel-good story so far. Heading into Saturday's game they had yet to concede a goal, but the one thing they had lacked was a home win - or even a home goal - after drawing blanks in stalemates with Hungary and Georgia in Belfast. They had already come close when Jamie Donley slotted home in the first half but the forward had strayed offside, leaving the moment the hosts had been waiting for to come through Devlin's superb winner. It leaves Northern Ireland's Nations League fate in their own hands, and a draw or better in Hungary would secure promotion to League A for the first time. For Northern Ireland boss Michael O'Neill, it was a huge moment from a player who he said is "a bit of a dream" to manage. "Terry's a great lad. He deserves everything he'll get from the game and he's one of those lads that maximises what he has," O'Neill said about the 23-year-old Portsmouth defender. Myotis septentrionalis Northern Long-eared Bat Image Details View Profile FWS Focus 415196 Northern long-eared Bat Tools and Resources On November 29, 2022 the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (Service) published a final rule to reclassify the northern long-eared bat (NLEB) as endangered under the Endangered Species Act. The species faces extinction due to the range-wide impacts of white-nose syndrome , a deadly disease affecting cave-dwelling bats across the continent. After considering feedback received on draft tools and technical assistance documents, we released final tools and documents on October 23, 2024. These tools and technical assistance documents were developed with the goal of providing Endangered Species Act compliance predictability across sectors and to demonstrate our commitment to proactively working with partners to conserve remaining NLEBs within their range while minimizing impacts to the regulated public. These tools also support the conservation of the proposed endangered tricolored bat (TCB), should the species be listed. Designation: National Heritage Area MANAGED BY: Northern Rio Grande National Heritage Area, Inc. The mountains and high desert of North Central New Mexico cradle the homelands of Native peoples, who have inhabited the area for thousands of years. Current descendants include the Jicarilla Apache Tribe and eight northern Pueblo settlements. The area comprising the Northern Río Grande National Heritage Area also includes descendants of Spanish colonists who settled in the area permanently, beginning in 1598, nearly two centuries before the signing of the Declaration of Independence. The district includes the upper Colorado River corridor along with the White and Yampa rivers. It is home to some of the largest deer and elk herds in the area, along with pronghorn, bighorn sheep and a wide variety of other wildlife. The Northwest District contains the majority of the Colorado range of the Greater Sage Grouse. The Northwest District also manages 7.1 million acres of subsurface minerals, which includes some of the most productive oil and natural gas fields in the state, four of Colorado’s nine coal mines and vast deposits of oil shale. In Bergen, the charming coastal capital, the Hanseatic Museum , which tells the story of the medieval Northern European merchant class, will reopen after a renovation, while the restaurant Gaptrast , which earned a second Michelin star in 2026, continues bringing the Nordic wilds to diners’ plates. The city will also be getting its own state-of-the-art boat in 2027 for nearby fjord cruises. Farther afield, visitors can venture on thrilling treks in national parks like Jostedalsbreen , capped by Europe’s biggest glacier , and Folgefonna . By Tabitha Britt Last updated June 11, 2025 • 9 min read Do multivitamins ensure your body gets everything it needs? It's a complicated question without a one-size-fits-all answer. While there’s no doubt taking multivitamins may benefit some people, experts suggest assessing your nutritional needs before popping a daily multivitamin. “A large amount of vitamins can cause nausea, vomiting, dehydration, confusion, and organ damage, such as [to the] liver or kidney,” says medical oncologist Liudmila Schafer. “Additionally, multivitamins containing certain minerals like calcium, magnesium, or zinc can interfere with the absorption of certain medications, such as antibiotics or thyroid medications.” ( How these two vitamin supplements could do more harm than good. ) That said, there are some situations in which a multivitamin may be helpful. pages.description: An easy way for Armed Forces personnel or their families to let IRS know they're in a combat zone.
pages.text: Notifying the IRS by Email about Combat Zone Service | Internal Revenue Service Skip to main content Notifying the IRS by Email about Combat Zone Service More In News Working Families Tax Cuts News releases Tax relief in disaster situations Topics in the news Fact sheets IRS statements and announcements IRS Tax Tips IRS guidance Media center Tax articles to share Posters to share Working with the Department of Defense, the Internal Revenue Service identifies taxpayers who are serving in a combat zone to suspend compliance actions, such as audits or enforced collections, until 180 days after the taxpayer has left the zone. Taxpayers, including civilian taxpayers working with U.S. Armed Forces, qualifying for such combat zone relief may also notify the IRS directly of their status through combatzone@irs.gov . They should provide their name, stateside address, date of birth, and the date of deployment to the combat zone. Taxpayers should also include any official document that indicates their area or military operation. Civilians usually provide a Letter of Authorization or a letter from their employer. However, letters from the military that state the taxpayer served in a tax-free zone or Combat Zone Tax Exclusion (CZTE) area are acceptable. Do not include any Social Security numbers in an email. The taxpayer, taxpayer's spouse, or an authorized agent or representative may make this notification. The IRS cannot provide tax account information by email. pages.description: Notre vaste et diverse communauté agit aux niveaux local, régional et mondial pour promouvoir notre vision d’un Internet pour tout le monde.
pages.text: Notre communauté - Internet Society Notre communauté Notre communauté Notre vaste et diverse communauté de plus de 150 000 bénévoles et 80 organisations apporte de véritables changements dans le monde entier. Ce réseau extraordinaire agit aux niveaux local, régional et mondial pour promouvoir notre vision d’un Internet ouvert, connecté à l’échelle mondiale, sécurisé et digne de confiance pour tout le monde. Qui compose notre communauté ? Membres individuels Nos membres individuels jouent un rôle essentiel dans la mise en œuvre de notre vision en contribuant à des projets menés par la communauté. Ils participent à des événements, des campagnes de plaidoyer et des initiatives d’autonomisation. Chapitres Nos chapitres accomplissent un travail remarquable (sur six continents !) pour répondre aux besoins de leurs communautés. Ils informent, sensibilisent et éduquent sur les enjeux liés à Internet, renforcent les capacités locales et favorisent la collaboration au sein des communautés. Groupes d’intérêts spéciaux (SIG) et groupes permanents (SG) Nos SIG et SG rassemblent des membres de l’Internet Society partageant les mêmes centres d’intérêt afin de travailler sur les enjeux liés à Internet qui leur tiennent le plus à cœur. Toute personne membre individuelle ou membre d’un chapitre peut rejoindre un SIG ou un SG. pages.description: Comment l’Internet Society œuvre à réduire la fracture numérique et à rétablir la confiance dans l’Internet mondial. Pour tout le monde.
pages.text: Notre travail - Internet Society Notre travail Notre travail Œuvrer pour un Internet fiable et communautaire, accessible à tout le monde. Internet est une force transformatrice. Mais tout le monde n’en bénéficie pas de la même manière. Environ 2 milliards de personnes n’ont toujours pas accès à Internet. Et, de plus en plus, notre sécurité en ligne est mise en péril par le manque de confiance quant au contrôle de nos informations personnelles. Les enjeux n’ont jamais été aussi importants. C’est pourquoi nous nous associons aux communautés pour aider chacun à surmonter ses obstacles spécifiques à la connectivité, qu’ils soient géographiques, techniques, réglementaires ou financiers. Dans le cadre de notre Stratégie 2030, nous nous concentrons sur deux défis mondiaux majeurs auxquels Internet est confronté : Manque de confiance envers Internet . Parce que tout le monde mérite une expérience Internet sûre, sécurisée et respectueuse de sa vie privée. Inégalités mondiales . Parce que les personnes du monde entier doivent avoir accès à un Internet abordable, fiable et résilient. Découvrez nos activités pour l’année à venir dans notre Plan d’action 2026 . The NOURISH Autoimmunity Digital Health Challenge is a competition to develop innovative digital applications to empower people with or at risk of autoimmune diseases. The tools will allow affected groups to easily monitor how daily diet and nutritional changes impact symptoms and immune health. NIH invites patients, dietitians, caregivers, and software developers to submit prototype digital tools. These include mobile apps, wearables, and AI systems. River Action UK has accused Natural Resources Wales (NRW) of not doing enough to assess or address any risk to local rivers and and other water bodies when plans for three farms in Powys were approved last year. It follows years of debate over the alleged impact of chicken farming on rivers such as the Wye and Severn - in an area dubbed the UK's "poultry capital" . NRW said it would be inappropriate to comment ahead of the court case, but that it would "participate fully in the legal process". The case is about plans to increase the capacity of three Powys farms by a combined 336,900 chickens, bringing the total to 522,000. The three farms are Neuadd Isaf, Rhosddu and Llanshay. Two of the farms, Rhosddu and Llanshay, are in the River Severn catchment while Neuadd Isaf is in the River Wye catchment. Waterman Term: April 1951 – June 1963 Field of science: Physics Biography of Alan T. Waterman The first director of NSF served two full terms from April 1951 through June 1963. "A quiet individual, a real scholar and decidedly effective in his quiet way, for everyone likes him and trusts him," was the way Vannevar Bush described Alan Waterman. Detlev Bronk, who chaired the NSB during Waterman's years as director, thought he was a "kind and gentle" man, but also someone who could be "firm and exacting ... and persistent in the fulfillment of his duties." Educated at Princeton University, Waterman received his doctorate in physics in 1916. After graduation, he taught physics at the University of Cincinnati. During World War I, his academic career was interrupted by two years with the Science and Research Division of the Army Signal Corps. He then returned to teaching, at Yale University, until the outbreak of World War II. His career with the government during the war included service with the National Defense Research Committee and the Office of Scientific Research and Development. In August 1946, he became deputy chief and chief scientist of the Office of Naval Research. Understanding those relationships requires researchers to combine data collected by different scientists, organizations, and agencies — often using different methods and formats. A $6.4 million NSF Established Program to Stimulate Competitive Research (NSF EPSCoR) award supported TickBase , a research, data science, and cyberinfrastructure project at the University of Idaho that brought together researchers from Idaho, Nevada, New Hampshire, and New Mexico to improve predictions of tick-borne disease patterns and dynamics. Through TickBase, researchers worked across institutions and disciplines to integrate disparate datasets and make them more findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable — the principles known as FAIR data. By connecting environmental, ecological, and disease data, the project enabled researchers to explore questions that would be difficult to answer with any single dataset. The project also created a lasting data resource that allows researchers to explore tick-related datasets and relationships. Through the new NSF National Quantum and Nanotechnology Infrastructure (NSF NQNI) program, NSF will support up to 16 sites over five years, providing students, researchers, and industry with access to state-of-the-art fabrication and characterization tools, instrumentation, and expertise. Together, the sites will form a shared national resource serving regional innovation ecosystems, including community colleges and small businesses. NSF NQNI will accelerate U.S. leadership in quantum information science and engineering, nanotechnology, semiconductors, biotechnology, advanced manufacturing, and other emerging technologies. "This NSF investment in research facilities will power U.S. discovery in quantum and nanotechnologies to fuel our economy," said Don Millard, head of Engineering at NSF. "With facilities open to students, faculty and small businesses, NQNI will enable transformative ideas to be explored, scaled, and translated." NSF X-Labs, a $1.5 billion initiative launched in May 2026 , is a decade-long commitment to tackle critical scientific and technological challenges through novel and innovative research partnerships. Computation at the Limit of Physics , the third of three X-Labs topics NSF previewed in September , aims to sharply narrow the gap between the energy efficiency of today's chip-based computing and the fundamental limits set by physics. The transistors in today's computer chips require energy to perform calculations. Since the mid-2000s, supply voltages have plateaued, constrained by the thermal limit on transistors, and gains in energy per operation have slowed sharply. This stagnation is unsustainable as computational demand, and with it energy consumption, grows faster than efficiency gains can offset. Maintaining U.S. leadership in semiconductors, data centers, high-performance computing, and super intelligence requires computation that uses far less energy than current consumption levels. pages.text: NSF statement on Executive Order: Ushering in the Next Frontier of Quantum Innovation | NSF - U.S. National Science Foundation Print this Page NSF News NSF statement on Executive Order: Ushering in the Next Frontier of Quantum Innovation June 22, 2026 The U.S. National Science Foundation supports the Administration’s commitment to securing American leadership in quantum information science and technology. This executive order reflects a clear-eyed recognition that quantum innovation is not a distant horizon — it is happening now, and the nation that leads this transition will define the future of computing, sensing, communications and national security. From the lab bench to the factory floor, from the classroom to the clean room, NSF's role in this executive order runs deep — advancing the basic research, national infrastructure and workforce development pipelines that turn quantum promise into quantum capability. That work is not new for NSF. What this order does is accelerate it. Across academia, government and industry, America has an unmatched array of brilliant people working on quantum science and technology. Too often they are working in silos. NSF is uniquely positioned — and now formally directed — to bring that talent together. We are ready.
